newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain had 376.5 bln pesetas January cash deficit.
newsitem.headline: Spain had 376.5 bln pesetas January cash deficit.

text.p: The Economy Ministry said on Wednesday that Spain's state cash deficit was 376.5 billion pesetas in January.
In January, 1996 the cash deficit was 151.9 billion pesetas.

In December, the cash deficit was 1,096.9 billion pesetas taking into account the surprise budget shortfall discovered in July 1996. It was 947.9 billion pesetas in December without taking into account the July shortfall.
The figures relate to central government finances only.
Spanish Budget Secretary Jose Folgado said the deterioration was due to technical factors.
"It doesn't have any importance because it's atypical," said Folgado.
"January data is not representative," he added.
Earlier this morning, Folgado said he was expecting a budget surplus in February.
Folgado explained that in January there were exceptional factors, which affect both the comparison and the actual data. So he said it was necessary to await a correction in the next months.
